sections.title: Chapter 1 — Linux and the System Administrator
1.9 The Role of a Linux System Administrator
1.10 Physical Servers, Virtual Machines, and Cloud Instances

workshop.problem: A website disappears after reboot: a successful manual launch was mistaken for a managed service.
An unquoted variable turns one intended filename into several arguments.
A deleted log still consumes space because a process retains its descriptor.
The same displayed name has different numeric ownership on a recovery host.
Making a file writable does not repair a missing search permission on its parent.
An update installs successfully but the service cannot read its configuration.
An arbitrary kill hides the symptom and destroys the evidence needed to explain it.
A unit is started manually but was never enabled for the intended boot target.
Free space on one filesystem does not help a different full mount.
A larger logical volume is reported while the mounted filesystem capacity stays unchanged.
A successful ping is mistaken for evidence that an HTTPS application works.
An SSH policy edit locks out the only working administrator session.

workshop.problem: A correct address is returned but the service is not listening on that endpoint.

workshop.problem: Logs from another boot are used to explain a current failure.
A scheduled job works interactively but fails with its different environment.
A failed pipeline leaves a partially written status page presented as current.
A broad permission change fixes one symptom while silently widening access.

sections.title: Chapter 20 — File Sharing and Network Storage

workshop.problem: A file appears with an unexpected owner because numeric identities differ.
A replica immediately copies an accidental deletion and has no recoverable earlier state.
A single high load average is treated as proof of CPU saturation.
A reinstall changes unrelated state before the failed layer is identified.
A kernel package update is assumed to change the running kernel without reboot.
A snapshot on the same lost storage is treated as disaster recovery.
Replacing a container discards state that was written only to its ephemeral layer.
A script appends the same configuration line each time it runs.

workshop.problem: The instance boots again but credentials and persistent-volume attachment are missing.
A green process-status indicator substitutes for the user-facing acceptance check.
A resource control is changed without measuring the contention it was intended to resolve.
A manual emergency fix becomes undocumented permanent fleet drift.
